title: Clean Module at a Host Call Site
statement: Let six finite Boolean Turing machines be given, padded to a common work-tape count $K$, and let $i\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$. Suppose module $i$ satisfies the clean-module contract with result function $f$, emission function $g$, and budget $B$. For every Boolean input $x$, argument word $\mathrm{arg}$, and output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$, there is a positive time $t\le B(|\mathrm{arg}|)$ such that the host, started at module $i$'s entry on $x$ with $\mathrm{arg}$ on tape zero, all other tapes blank, and output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$, does not reach the loop-anchor state at any time before $t$, and at time $t$ is in the module's return state with $f(\mathrm{arg})$ on tape zero, all other tapes blank, and output $\mathrm{pre}\,g(\mathrm{arg})$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a family of six finite Boolean Turing machines
each machine's work-tape count is at most $K$
functions $f,g$ from Boolean words to Boolean words
module $i$ satisfies the clean-module contract with $f,g,B$
replaced:
Let the $i$-th module of the host satisfy the clean-module contract with result
$f$, emission $g$, and budget $B$. Then for every native input, argument, and
output prefix, there is a positive time within $B$ of the argument length during
which the host, started at that module's entry, avoids the loop anchor and then
reaches the module's return state over the state word of $f$ of the argument,
with $g$ of the argument appended to the output.
